neighbours.label: the perfect auxiliary (has/have) in the result clause that follows an instruction in a how-to ('you'll notice that the stretch has moved', 'you will see that the mixture has started to foam')
fire: Tighten the last bolt and you'll see that the frame has stopped wobbling.
After the fifth rinse, you will notice that the water has turned clear.
Leave the dough for an hour and you'll find it has doubled in size.
Run the test again and you should see that the error has disappeared.
Press the pedal gently; you'll feel that the clutch has started to bite.
Once the paint dries, notice how the colour has deepened.
Reload the page and you'll see that the counter has reset to zero.
Breathe out slowly and you will notice that your shoulders have dropped.
quiet: Tighten the last bolt and you'll see that the frame stops wobbling.
After the fifth rinse, you will notice that the water runs clear.
Leave the dough for an hour and then shape it into a loaf.
Run the test again and check the log for errors.
My neighbour has moved to a flat nearer the station.
The council has started to repaint the railings along the river.
The counter on the website has reset to zero overnight.
Her shoulders have dropped since she began the exercises.

predictions: Fire items 0.4-0.6 peaking on ' has'/' have'; instruction frames with the simple present under 0.05; narrative perfects outside a how-to are the real test and may leak to 0.2-0.4.
notes: Card: 'And with that we've got it - we have calculated' (-66), 'you'll notice that the noodle will', 'The tension has moved up', 'Check that there are', 'Assert we called', 'You have just pulled'; the + pole suppresses have/has/had/'ve.
